import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/test_10.csv"
]

# Step 1: Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
# Each CSV has a header and an index column (the first column) which should be ignored (index_col=0)
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_files]

# Step 2: All source tables have the same schema ['0'], and the target schema is also ['0'].
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, since all source tables share the same schema as the target,
# we should UNION (concatenate) all source tables vertically.

# Step 3: Concatenate all DataFrames
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 4: Ensure the column '0' is integer type as per target schema
target_df['0'] = target_df['0'].astype(int)

# Step 5: Write the result to the specified target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
